input.quote: (a) General Servicing Obligations. The Servicer will manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures.
input.rationale: The transaction contains the functional equivalent of the performance warranty package and it meets (indeed exceeds) the preferred position on the material terms. Quality standard: Section 3.2(a) binds Cellco as Servicer to service with reasonable care using the degree of skill and attention it applies to comparable receivables it services for itself or others under the Servicing Procedures — the securitization analogue of "professional and workmanlike." Conformance warranty and duration: the Eligibility Representation is made by each Originator and the Servicer as of the Closing Date and each Acquisition Date and expressly "will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Receivables" and the pledge to the Indenture Trustee (p0069/p0071), as do the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's Section 6.1 representations (p0257) — i.e., open-ended survival rather than the preferred 12-month/90-day windows. Remedy: Section 2.5(b)-(c) requires the Originator to reacquire, or the Servicer to acquire, any Receivable for which the Eligibility Representation was breached (uncured, material adverse effect), and Section 3.3(b) requires the Servicer to acquire Receivables where it fails to cure a breach of its Section 3.2(c)/(d) obligations, in each case at the Acquisition Amount (present value of the Principal Balance net of collections) — a cash refund-equivalent remedy after a cure period, which satisfies the "repair, replace or refund" element. Compliance-with-law warranties are present (No Violation / No Conflict). No "AS IS" clause or blanket warranty disclaimer appears anywhere; Section 6.2(a)'s limitation to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence preserves the parties' "specific obligations," so the reacquisition/acquisition remedy is not swallowed — and that liability standard is a limitation-of-liability point addressed under the LOL rule, not double-flagged here. The absence of documentation-conformance and malicious-code warranties is not material in a receivables transfer and servicing agreement (no software or deliverables). No redline proposed.
